item.title: Trump hails Infantino as USA to co-host 2031 Women’s World Cup
item.description: President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup. Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in July with a shortlived plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A FIFA election next March in Morocco will decide if Infantino keeps his job against rival contenders Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan. “Thank you to Gianni Infantino, and his great staff, for working to bring the Tournament to the USA,” Trump posted on social media. Trump and Infantino awarded Spain the trophy at this year’s final of the World Cup, which was co-hosted by Canada and Mexico. FIFA confirmed Monday that the United States will co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after Infantino noted it was the “sole candidacy” for the tournament. “I am proud to announce that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will take place in the United States!” Trump posted. “After hosting the Most Successful World Cup in History, no Country is better positioned than the United States to be home to the largest Women’s Sporting Event in History.” The Women’s World Cup field will expand to a record 48 teams in 2031. “The FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will bring Generational Economic Impact to the United States, grow the sport of Soccer throughout our Country and the World, and showcase America’s Exceptionalism,” Trump posted. item.title: 2027: ‘No Political Ambition Is Worth The Life Of A Nigerian’, IGP Warns Politicians
item.description: The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Tuesday warned politicians against turning the 2027 general elections into a theatre of violence. Speaking at a high-level security meeting in Abuja with the Independent National Electoral Commission, political party leaders, civil society organisations and other stakeholders, Disu described the growing incidents of political violence as a serious threat to public peace and democratic participation. He warned politicians to desist from violence, which has led to growing cases of reported killings across the country. “We are meeting at a particularly critical moment in our nation’s democratic journey. Recent incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and convoys, the use of dangerous weapons, intimidation of political opponents and the disruption of lawful political gatherings have become matters of serious concern. “These developments threaten public peace, endanger innocent lives and undermine confidence in our democratic institutions. They are warning signs that must be addressed decisively before they escalate into a broader threat to national security. “ Let me state categorically that political competition must never become a justification for violence. Democracy provides an opportunity for citizens to freely express their political preferences, support candidates of their choice and hold differing opinions without fear or intimidation. “It must never become a contest of who can mobilise more thugs, deploy more weapons or inflict greater harm on political opponents. No political ambition is worth the life of a Nigerian, and no electoral victory is worth the destruction of our national peace.” The IGP noted that the Force would not tolerate political violence, warning to take legal actions on those found guilty of employing thugs to intimidate and assault the public. “The position of the Nigeria Police Force is clear: we have zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the political party, candidate, personality or interest involved. Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable. “We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not to any political party or individual. We will protect the rights of all lawful political actors to organise rallies, hold meetings and participate in the democratic process. “However, we will not hesitate to take lawful and decisive action against anyone who engages in thuggery, intimidation, assault, the use of offensive weapons or any conduct capable of disrupting public peace. “I wish to remind all political actors that the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the INEC Regulations and other applicable laws prescribe clear standards of conduct and consequences for electoral offences. “Political office, party affiliation or personal influence does not place anyone above the law. item.title: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: My dad died from fake drugs — IMAN president
item.description: ……IMAN to introduce TIN for importers in 2027 By Efe Onodjae & Jacintha Ezugwu The President of the Importers Association of Nigeria (IMAN), George Ndubuisi, has said his personal experience of losing his father to fake drugs has strengthened his resolve to fight the importation and distribution of counterfeit and adulterated products in Nigeria. Ndubuisi, who disclosed that his father died in 2013 after taking drugs he described as fake, said the association would introduce an importer identification number in February 2027 to ensure that every imported container and its contents could be traced to a particular individual. He said this during an end of the year party with the association at the Apapa office, Lagos. According to him the initiative was designed to hold importers accountable for prohibited and substandard goods entering the country, while protecting clearing agents from bearing the consequences of import violations committed by their clients. The IMAN president said the proposed system would ensure that every container brought into the country was linked to a specific importer through shipping documents and other relevant records. He said, “In February 2027, IMAN is going to take a new position because the goalpost determines where you will put the goal. “We are shifting the goalpost to ensure that every container or import that comes into the country is tagged to a particular person. That gives room for an IMAN identification number, through which every importer registered on our platform is a confirmed importer. “If you are not on our platform, you are not an importer.” Ndubuisi said the initiative became necessary because some importers allegedly bring prohibited goods, including arms and ammunition, into the country without proper identification. He lamented that when such consignments are intercepted by the Nigeria Customs Service, clearing agents often bear the consequences while the importers disappear. He said the proposed identification system would make it difficult for importers to evade responsibility, adding that their identities would be traceable through shipping documents. “Even in the case of a breach, when Customs holds the goods, the people who suffer are the agents, while the importers go into hiding. “With this measure, we want to bring the importer to book. Even if you try to hide, your identity on the shipping documents represents who you are,” he said. The IMAN president explained that the identification number would be linked to the bank account of the importer, making it easier to establish ownership of imported goods and trace individuals responsible for bringing substandard products into the country. He said the system would also help identify importers involved in the importation of fake and adulterated products, which he described as a major threat to public health and the economy. item.title: Pete Edochie: Fans mourn Nollywood legend, recall iconic roles
item.description: Social media users and fans of veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, have taken to social media to mourn his death, describing it as the “loss of an iconic figure in Nigeria’s film industry”. His death was announced by his family in a statement shared on Instagram by his eldest son, Leo Edochie, through his account, @Edochieleo, on Wednesday. The statement said Edochie died in the early hours of Wednesday in Enugu after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. The actor’s death at 79 has attracted tributes, from fans with social media users recalling his memorable performances, distinctive voice and contribution to Nollywood. A fan, @UrchiL, described Edochie’s death as the loss of a legend, saying, “Things have really fallen apart, Nollywood has really lost a legend and an iroko. Rip Pete Edochie we would miss your legendary voice and proverbs in Nollywood movies.” Another fan, @chinedu, wrote, “An iroko has truly fallen. Rest easy legend.” @Adeyanju, described the actor as a giant whose death had deeply affected him, saying, “Indeed, Things Have Fallen Apart and the heavens have come to Collect!! This one pain me oh!!” @Brianjude wrote, “Rest in Peace Odogwu Chief Pete Edochie.” A user, @Rexemmy4, also lamented the actor’s death, saying, “Rest in peace Ebubedike. Sadly, 2026 has taken almost the whole Igwe council in Nollywood, and now it has even taken the Igwe too. Only the bodyguards remain now.” @Tobelani15 recalled the actor’s plans for his 80th birthday, saying he had mentioned the plans during an interview on Curiosity. @Tidal described Edochie’s life as fulfilled, saying his death should be celebrated while extending condolences to his family. Edochie was widely celebrated for his portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart, which brought him national and international recognition. (NAN) The post Pete Edochie: Fans mourn Nollywood legend, recall iconic roles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kwankwasiyya Supporters Carry Sticks But Harm Nobody, Obi Clarifies ‘Rig And Die’ Slogan
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified controversies surrounding the popular ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone. He spoke in an interview with Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State, after an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting. Addressing concerns over the presence of weapons at political gatherings, Obi said the public had misunderstood the ‘rig and die’ calls against electoral malpractice as opposition to political campaigns. This is as he defended supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, over allegations that they carry sticks to political campaigns, saying the items have not been used to “harm anyone”. Obi insisted that he had not witnessed anyone being attacked with the stick-wielding Kwankwasiyya movement during political gatherings. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” he said. Obi explained that the Kwankwasiyya movement, led by Kwankwaso, had a longstanding tradition of supporters appearing at political gatherings with sticks and similar items. He said, “Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody. “I’ve been part of that family for a while, and I’ve never seen one day, maybe behind me, that anybody was harmed because they were carrying such items.” The former Anambra State governor appealed to security agencies and other authorities to prevent violence during political activities, warning against the loss of lives over political ambitions. “So we’re pleading with the authorities. Please, we cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders,” he added. His comments came amid growing concerns over attacks on opposition political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. On Monday, gunmen attacked a campaign gathering of the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, leaving several people dead and others injured. Omo-Agege, a former Deputy President of the Senate, escaped the attack, while members of his campaign team and other supporters were among the casualties. item.title: What I want to be remembered for – Pete Edochie
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku When Pete Edochie turned 76 in 2023, he revealed what he would want to be remembered for when he’s no more. In a chat with Vanguard to mark his 76th birthday, Ebubedike, as he was fondly called by his friends and colleagues in the movie industry, said he would like to be remembered as that man who brought happiness and joy to many homes in Africa and beyond with his craft. Edochie became famous after the iconic role he played as Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s best-selling novel, “Things Fall Apart”, in the 80s. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential actors in the African film industry, having spent more than 50 years of his life bringing happiness to many homes in Africa and beyond. item.title: Ronaldo deserves fitting farewell from Portugal, says Guardiola
item.description: Pep Guardiola has called on the Portuguese Football Federation to give Cristiano Ronaldo a fitting farewell from the national team, saying the forward deserves to end his international career with the recognition of his country. The former Manchester City manager made the appeal during an interview with former Brazilian footballer Romário on Tuesday, following Ronaldo’s announcement of his retirement from international football earlier this month. “Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn’t leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can’t let him go like this,” Guardiola said. “Both sides need to make an effort to guarantee a fitting farewell. He’s been an incredibly important figure, not only for himself and Portugal, but for future generations of Portuguese players.” He added that Ronaldo’s achievements deserved to be celebrated rather than overshadowed by a disagreement with members of the national team. “An entire career shouldn’t be judged based on a month or two, or because of a disagreement or misunderstanding with one or two individuals,” he said. “There are exceptional players, and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified.” Guardiola also called for a celebration in which Ronaldo would feel appreciated by Portuguese supporters, urging both parties to put their differences behind them. “There should be a celebration where he feels the love of his countrymen, and he, in turn, must also take the initiative and say: Let’s turn the page on the past,” he added. The disagreement between Ronaldo and Jesus came to public attention on September 30, when the forward left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen ahead of their Nations League fixture against Denmark. Ronaldo had been an unused substitute in Portugal’s 2-1 victory over Norway on September 27, despite warming up for about 30 minutes during the match. Jesus later admitted that Ronaldo was unhappy with his decision not to introduce him, while the forward subsequently accused the coach of breaking his word over an agreement concerning his playing time and the explanation of his omission. Ronaldo also apologised for his conduct following the incident but said he remained available for Portugal after serving any punishment imposed by the football authorities. However, on November 5, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a 23-year career with the national team. In his announcement, Ronaldo said it was time to hand back Portugal’s iconic No. 7 shirt, adding that the decision was not easy because it involved both his head and his heart. He finished his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, making him the most-capped player and highest goalscorer in men’s international football. Following his retirement, the Portuguese Football Federation redesigned the national team’s No. 7 shirt in tribute to the forward. item.title: Can We Prepare Children For Financial Success Before They Start Earning?
item.description: Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation. In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa. Why should financial education begin in childhood? Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children? Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions? A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly. Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early. Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day. The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions. The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely. We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master. item.title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations. Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.” In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry. “Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said. He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions. “He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said. Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart. The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema. Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs. His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji. In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours. item.title: Taraba youths assure Tinubu of peaceful reception ahead of campaign visit
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — Youths and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Taraba State have assured President Bola Tinubu of a peaceful reception ahead of his anticipated campaign visit to the state for the 2027 general elections. The youths, who also declared their readiness to mobilise support for the President and other APC candidates, made the pledge during a solidarity road walk in Tella Town, Wuryo Ward, Gassol Local Government Area. They also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for appointing Taraba indigenes to strategic positions in his administration. The convener of the road walk and Senior Special Assistant to Governor Agbu Kefas on Youth Mobilisation, Hon. Acho Righteous, described the turnout as evidence of growing support for the APC and its preparedness for the 2027 elections. Righteous commended the APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, for strengthening the party’s national structure and advancing its unification agenda, particularly in Taraba, which recently transitioned from PDP to APC leadership. “Our National Chairman, the erudite Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has rebuilt the party and we are solidly behind his unification agenda. “We are now on the field and mobilising our people to ensure President Bola Tinubu, Governor Agbu Kefas and all APC candidates at the state and national levels win convincingly at the polls,” he said. He also praised the APC State Chairman, Abubakar Bawa, for promoting unity and strengthening the party’s structures across the state. The Commissioner for Science and Technology, Hon. Muslim Aruwa, and an APC chieftain, Alhaji Adamu Musa, who also spoke at the event, said the road walk demonstrated the party’s determination to consolidate its grassroots support ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Pete Edochie: Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence — Pat Utomi
item.description: Political economist, Pat Utomi, has paid tribute to veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as a cultural institution whose legacy will endure beyond his lifetime. Utomi, in a tribute shared on his Facebook page on Wednesday, said Nigeria had lost a distinguished voice whose contributions to the country’s entertainment industry and cultural heritage would remain unforgettable. Describing Edochie as an iroko tree that had fallen, Utomi said the veteran actor’s departure was a monumental loss not only to the entertainment industry but also to generations who grew up watching his performances. “An iroko has fallen, Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence,” he wrote. He described Edochie as a custodian of African storytelling and a cultural institution whose commanding presence and performances had become part of Nigeria’s collective memory. Utomi particularly recalled the actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart, saying he brought the character to life and presented the depth and complexities of African civilisation to the world. “When Chief Pete Edochie stood before the camera as Okonkwo in Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, he did something extraordinary. He breathed life into a literary character and gave the world a glimpse into the depth, complexity, pride and contradictions of African civilisation,” he said. According to Utomi, Edochie did not merely interpret the character but immortalised it through his performance. He noted that the actor’s distinctive voice, commanding presence and dignified approach to his craft had earned him a special place in the hearts of audiences across generations. Beyond acting, Utomi acknowledged Edochie’s contributions to Nigerian broadcasting and cinema, saying his influence extended beyond entertainment and helped shape the country’s cultural landscape. He added that although the actor’s departure marked the end of a remarkable chapter, his legacy would continue through his films, the stories passed down to younger generations and the inspiration he provided to emerging actors. Utomi also extended his condolences to Edochie’s wife, children, family, friends and colleagues, praying that God would grant them the strength to bear the loss. “May your soul find eternal rest. Rest well, EBUBEDIKE!! Nigeria will never forget your legacy, Africa will speak your name till the end of time,” he added. item.title: 10 Things to Know About Late Nollywood Veteran Pete Edochie
item.description: The Nigerian entertainment industry has been thrown into mourning following the death of veteran Nollywood actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, who died at the age of 79 on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Edochie, renowned for his commanding screen presence, distinctive voice and memorable portrayal of traditional rulers and family patriarchs, was one of the most recognisable figures in Nigerian cinema. Here are 10 things to know about the late actor. 1. He was born in Zaria, Kaduna State Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, although he hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. He grew up in northern Nigeria before eventually establishing his roots in the southeastern part of the country. 2. He started his career as a broadcaster Before becoming a household name in Nollywood, Edochie built a career in broadcasting. He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant and gradually rose through the ranks. He later became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, where he also served as Deputy Managing Director and occasionally as Acting Managing Director. 3. He became famous for playing Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart One of the defining moments of Edochie’s career was his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s celebrated novel, Things Fall Apart . His performance as the proud and uncompromising Igbo warrior earned him widespread recognition and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading television actors. The role also attracted international attention, including coverage by the British Broadcasting Corporation. 4. He featured in over 200 screen productions Edochie went on to feature in numerous Nigerian films and television productions throughout his career. Some of his notable works include Rituals , Igodo , Billionaire’s Club , Egg of Life and Lionheart . In Genevieve Nnaji’s 2018 film Lionheart , he played Chief Ernest Obiagu. 5. He was known for his deep voice and African proverbs One of the qualities that distinguished Edochie from many actors was his commanding voice and measured delivery. He became particularly associated with characters who portrayed traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen, fathers and authoritative family patriarchs. His frequent use of African proverbs and traditional expressions also became a defining feature of his performances, earning him admiration among generations of movie lovers. 6. He received the national honour of MON In recognition of his contributions to Nigerian entertainment, Edochie received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003. He also received the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Africa Film Academy. item.title: “We’ve lost a titan, legend, an icon,” Gov Mbah mourns Pete Edochie
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the passing on of one of Nollywood’s greatest, Chief Pete Edochie, describing it as the departure of a giant, icon, and patriot. Mbah further described it as a personal loss to Enugu State, recalling that although the renown thespian hailed from Nteje in Anambra State, he had unequivocally acknowledged his life-long ties with Enugu State, which he had often described as his birth place, his “first port of call,” and a home away from home. The Governor, in his personal tribute to Edochie in the early hours of Wednesday, following the announcement of the actor’s demise, aged 79, by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, further explained that the deceased was a great ambassador of Enugu State and fan of his administration. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of Chief Pete Edochie, one of Nigeria’s most iconic actors and titans, and one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood and Africa’s creative industry across the world. “The pain of this loss is further deepened by its timing. It comes at a particularly poignant moment when Enugu, a city whose history and identity are deeply intertwined with the arts, is hosting the National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST). “At a time when we are celebrating the richness of our cultural heritage and the creative talents that give it expression, we are confronted with the loss of one of its most distinguished ambassadors. It is a sobering reminder that while we celebrate the enduring power of our arts and culture, we must also mourn those who gave them life and brought them global recognition. “Pete Edochie was more than an accomplished actor; he was an institution. With his commanding screen presence, unmistakable voice, remarkable mastery of dialogue and profound understanding of his craft, he helped shape the identity of Nigerian cinema and took the stories, values and cultural expressions of our people to audiences across the world. As an illustrious son of the South East, and dating back to his role as a tragic protagonist in the dramatization of Chinua Achebe’s 1958 novel, ‘Things Fall Apart,’ Edochie eloquently interpreted the society to the world. He wore his Igbo identity with pride, bringing its language, wisdom, proverbs and rich cultural heritage to life in ways that resonated far beyond our shores. “His performances transcended entertainment, preserving aspects of our cultural heritage and inspiring generations of actors and storytellers. “His was a career defined not merely by longevity but by excellence, distinction and enduring influence and uncommon social grace. “Even as the curtain falls on this remarkable life, his legacy as a fine broadcaster, thespian, cultural ambassador, and super star will continue to live on in the countless lives he touched and the generations of performers he inspired. “Although this is a personal loss to us as Ndi Enugu, my heart, nevertheless, particularly goes out to his immediate household. item.title: Paris Club Refunds: ‘We have no hands in transaction’ – Nigeria Governors’ Forum
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – THE Nigeria Governors’ Forum, the umbrella body of the 36 state governors has denied having transactions with regard to the N135.5 billion paid to the forum as stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute. Read Also: Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum The NGF said it did not engage any party thereto, nor held any such monies in its custody at any time. The governors made the clarification in a statement signed very late yesterday night by Director Media and Strategic Communications NGF, Yunusa Tanko Abdullahi. It was in reaction to reports on the Federal Capital Territory Court interim order freezing N135.5 billion linked to Governors’ Forum and restraining 29 banks. The Forum said: “The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) is aware of recent media reports regarding the November 19, 2026 interim order, obtained exparte, issued by the Federal High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja in the Paris Club refund suit filed by Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards from events that happened in 2016. “Please note that this issue emanated from allegations of transactions between the plaintiff and the Association of Local Government of Nigeria, ALGON. The Nigeria Governors Forum has no hand in that transaction and did not engage any party thereto, nor held any such monies in its custody at any time. “Meanwhile, the NGF’s legal team is currently reviewing the court processes and will respond accordingly. The Forum reiterates its unwavering commitment to the rule of law, transparency and accountability.” Abuja High Court order Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte application brought by Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards. The order restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the funds. The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF within their custody. The judge further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of service, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the disputed funds. The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and amounts preserved under the court’s order. The amount represents 100 million dollar, equivalent to the N135.55 billion, calculated at the exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar. Justice Agbaza made the orders on November 19, following the ex parte application and submissions by the claimant’s Counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, alongside Damilola Odesola, from Ade Okeaya-Inneh & Co. item.title: Emir of Daura suspended
item.description: The Katsina State Government has suspended the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar, from all official engagements pending the outcome of an investigation into allegations of sexual assault made against him by a foreign female tourist. The emir, who was also barred from travelling, has been confined to the inner chambers of the palace as police took over the premises. Daily Trust gathered that the most senior councillor in the Daura Emirate Council, the Galadiman Daura and District Head of Mai’adua, is expected to assume responsibility for the emir’s official functions and oversee the affairs of the traditional institution during the period of his suspension. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, had alleged in a video that went viral on Sunday that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts during a visit to the palace as part of her tour of Nigeria. The woman explained that despite cautioning the monarch, he persisted, beaming with smiles. She said although the incident occurred on November 14, she chose not to make it public until she had completed her tour and left the country. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. In a statement on Tuesday by the Katsina State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu Zango, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda expressed displeasure over the emir’s alleged conduct and constituted a committee to investigate the allegation and advise the government accordingly. “Meanwhile, the state government has also suspended all official engagements and travels of the monarch. The government wishes to assure the public that justice will be served and that the outcome of the committee’s findings and recommendations will be fully implemented. “Therefore, the government wishes to call on the general public to be calm, law-abiding and continue with their normal activities,” the statement added. item.title: No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports alleging that $2.04 billion realised from crude oil cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for, insisting that all transactions were fully reconciled. The company said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were set off against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to Nigeria under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme. In a statement by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, NNPC said the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes did not indicate missing funds. “No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” it stated. Under the DSDP programme, participating traders lifted crude oil in exchange for refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market. NNPC explained that while crude was priced in dollars, products supplied were sold in naira, with transactions reconciled and captured in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. The company said all 59 cargoes referenced in the reports were accounted for, adding that 30 were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then designated Federal Inland Revenue Service dollar account. On Duke Oil’s ownership, NNPC said it was incorporated in 1989 as its wholly owned trading subsidiary, adding that the relationship was documented in its corporate history, audited financial statements and NEITI’s 2023 industry report. It maintained that transactions between the company and its subsidiaries were disclosed as related-party transactions under International Financial Reporting Standards. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, but warned that it reserved the right to take legal action against publications it considered false or misleading. item.title: Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79
item.description: Pete Edochie, Nollywood legend, has died at the age of 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Chief Edochie died at 12:30a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, the family announced. Read Also: Pete Edochie’s exclusive interview with Vanguard and reaction to death rumours in February His family made the announcement in a statement on Instagram by Leo Pete Edochie, his son, describing the late veteran actor as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman”. He captioned the post “An Iroko Has Fallen.” “With profound sadness and hearts bowed in total submission to the will of Almighty God, we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE, MON (Ononenyi), a retired broadcaster and veteran Actor,” the statement read. Edochie “departed this life on Wednesday, 25th November 2026 at 12.30a.m. after a protracted battle with prostate cancer in Enugu, Nigeria. He was aged 79 years. “Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE hailed from Akamnato Ifite Nteje and is survived by his beloved wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, his children, siblings and numerous other relations. “Funeral arrangements will be announced in due course. “As we mourn this painful loss, we pray that Almighty God grants his gentle soul eternal rest and gives the entire family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. “May God be with us all at this trying time,” added. Below is the post: View this post on Instagram A post shared by Leo Edochie (@edochieleo) Biography Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. He attended St Patrick’s and St James Primary Schools in Zaria; then St John’s College, Kaduna. Late Edochie studied journalism and television at the School of Journalism and Television in England. He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant. He rose through the ranks. He became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, then served as Deputy Managing Director, while occasionally acting as Managing Director. Things Fall Apart When the Nigerian Television Authority, NTA, adapted Chinua Achebe’s “Things Fall Apart” into a movie in 1987, Edochie’s portrayal of the protagonist Okonkwo, made him a household name in entertainment and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading actors. He has featured in many Nollywood movies, and won several awards. Vanguard News The post Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79 appeared first on Vanguard News .
